clue.text: Like an impossible clue, accepting end of crossword is unable to be cracked

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a clue nobody can solve is insoluble

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles that a clue is so hard it can never be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' opens the impossible-clue word after its first two letters to take in D, the final letter of crossword, plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indissoluble cannot be broken up or dissolved, as a bond that can never be cracked.

clue.text: Drunk, elbowing wife aside — that's contemptible

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the remaining letters are jumbled
putting something aside sets it apart, so this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A drunk shoving people out of the way, with his wife pushed aside, behaves contemptibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aside' removes W from ELBOWING, leaving ELBOING; 'Drunk' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble behaviour is base and dishonourable, deserving scorn.

clue.text: Have last of cheeseboard on top of port

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: on top of something is over it

explanation.surface: A diner finishes the cheeseboard and follows it with a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink after cheese, but it is the harbour town. DOVER is a ferry port on the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is a harbour town in Kent, England's main ferry crossing to France.

clue.text: Glimpse fortune-teller and tourist

parts.note: a glimpse is a sight of something
a seer foretells the future

explanation.surface: A visitor catches sight of a fortune-teller on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer is a visitor who goes around viewing famous places.

clue.text: Grain used as ingredient of goat stew

indicators.note: ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook adds some cereal to a stew made from goat meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal crop whose seeds are eaten as porridge or fed to horses.

clue.text: Support below leg

parts.note: below means under
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: Something holding a structure up beneath one of its legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to prop up a structure from beneath, hence to bolster or reinforce.

clue.text: Braille transcribed without the French sign

indicators.note: transcribing rewrites something in another form, so the letters are rearranged
without signals that some letters are left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Text turned into Braille but missing a French symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAILLE's letters are the answer plus LE; 'transcribed' rearranges them, 'without' takes LE away.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve zodiac signs.

clue.text: Police officer very tough in this area

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector, a British police rank
strict means stern and demanding

explanation.surface: A hard-line cop claims to be the toughest in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or neighbourhood marked off for administration.

clue.text: Hello John: this is a robbery

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
Jack is a familiar form of the name John

explanation.surface: A robber greets a victim by name before announcing a stick-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijack is the seizure of a vehicle or its cargo by force, a kind of theft.

clue.text: Negotiated passage, putting bed back outside

indicators.note: outside puts the reversed bed around the other piece
back means the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed
a gate is a way through, a passage

explanation.surface: Someone getting a bed through a narrow passage, pushing it in backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'outside' act on the bed word. 'Negotiated passage' looks like the definition, but 'passage' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate a route is to steer a way through it, as a ship or driver does.

clue.text: Litre in wine store I needed for this: it usually goes with caviar

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a bin is a rack for storing wine bottles

explanation.surface: A recipe asking for a litre from the wine cellar to serve with caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes traditionally topped with sour cream and caviar.

clue.text: Some collaborated to make compound

indicators.note: some of a word is a part of it, so the answer sits inside the word

explanation.surface: Chemists working together to produce a compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A borate is a salt of boric acid, a chemical compound containing boron.

clue.text: Macerate bats to make Cornish treat?

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Soaking flying mammals to produce a West Country delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the creatures being soaked; it is the adjective meaning mad. The '?' marks the definition as an example: Cornwall, in southwest England, is famous for scones with jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea of scones, jam and clotted cream with tea is a classic Cornish indulgence.

clue.text: Logo of famous stadium, naked male

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: Wembley is the national football stadium in London

explanation.surface: A club badge featuring a famous ground and a nude man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips W and Y from WEMBLEY, England's national football stadium, leaving EMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbol or badge representing an organisation, much like a trademark design.

clue.text: Might one be duelling, with strings attached?

definitions.text: Might one be duelling, with strings attached?

parts.words: Might one be duelling, with strings attached?
parts.note: Duelling Banjos is a famous bluegrass tune played by two pickers; strings attached hints at a stringed instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'with strings attached' suggests conditions on a deal, but the strings belong to an instrument, and the duel is the famous tune Duelling Banjos.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist plays the banjo, a stringed instrument, as in the tune Duelling Banjos.

clue.text: Stupid person picks pocket, getting credit

parts.note: to dip is slang for picking pockets
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A dim thief who robs pockets and then gets credit for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a fool or idiot.

clue.text: Appear so upset about old long-running series

indicators.note: about places the jumbled letters around the other piece
upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Viewers look distressed by an ancient TV show that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles APPEAR SO, and 'about' puts those letters around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a television or radio drama serial that runs for years.

clue.text: The last of these may be paid on spec, with time and sympathy, initially

definitions.text: The last of these may be paid

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone's final dues get paid speculatively, with a little sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last of these may be paid' plays on the phrase paying one's last respects at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Mourners pay their last respects to the dead, showing esteem at a funeral.

clue.text: What hot weather does to tomatoes and other items?

definitions.text: What hot weather does to tomatoes
definitions.meaning: the heat of sunshine dehydrates tomatoes, making them sun-dried

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words describing a sunny day's effect on tomatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small things too minor to list separately.

clue.text: Undersea craft permitted to be rented out again

parts.note: a sub is a submarine
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A submarine allowed to be leased to a second tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: To sublet is for a tenant to lease property to someone else in turn.

clue.text: Criminal tears around hotel grounds

indicators.note: around places the scrambled letters about the other piece
criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Hotel is the radio code word for H

explanation.surface: A crook ripping through the gardens of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges TEARS, and 'around' puts that about H.
explanation.definitionFit: To earth an electrical device is to ground it, a connection to the soil.

clue.text: Crushes other half's offspring

definitions.meaning: the child of one's partner from a previous relationship

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words meaning treads on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son by an earlier partner; other half is a jokey term for spouse.

clue.text: This fires deadly missiles — that sucks! No, just the opposite!

definitions.text: This fires deadly missiles — that sucks! No, just the opposite!

parts.words: This fires deadly missiles — that sucks! No, just the opposite!
parts.note: a hunting tube shoots poison darts by breath; the opposite of sucking is pushing air out

explanation.walkthrough: 'that sucks' reads as slang for bad news, but taken literally the weapon does the reverse of sucking.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which darts are propelled by a puff of breath.

clue.text: The end of war, it's said, is such a small thing

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is spoken and heard rather than written

parts.note: peace is what comes when fighting ends

explanation.surface: The ending of a conflict is said to be a trivial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of war' looks like a call for the last letter, R; it is a whole phrase meaning the ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a fragment or bit, a small part of something.

clue.text: Sweet creature, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word spoken rather than written

parts.note: a mouse is a small creature

explanation.surface: Someone hears a cute little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the cute creature; it is the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light, airy dessert, a pudding Britons call a sweet.

clue.text: Sees us hiding, eating Japanese food

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Someone spots us in our hiding place as we eat Japanese food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Soldier, perhaps, I will be against

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant, so an ant is an example of a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier declares opposition to the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier, perhaps' suggests a military person, but soldier ants are a caste in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means opposed to something, as a preposition.

clue.text: Follow east, north, south, then head to Uruguay, east

indicators.note: head to takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Directions for a zigzag journey ending in Uruguay.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, so to happen next.

clue.text: Swindle official count, one might say, to get unanimity

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle

indicators.note: one might say signals a word spoken aloud

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population

explanation.surface: Rigging the official count to make everyone seem to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general agreement among a whole group.

clue.text: Destroy pirates (RIP)? No sweat!

indicators.note: destroying something breaks it up, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A sea battle cry: wipe out the buccaneers, rest in peace, easy job!
explanation.walkthrough: 'No sweat' reads as easy; 'No' joins the fodder and 'sweat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiration is the moisture the skin exudes, the same as sweat.
